title: Resource Estimation for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Programs
authors: Bonan Su, Yuan Feng, Li Zhou, Mingsheng Ying
abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computation enables the deployment of practical quantum algorithms but incurs substantial overhead from error correction, making resource estimation a central concern. Beyond case-by-case analyses, existing quantum programming languages either require programmers to manipulate low-level hardware details, rendering fault-tolerant implementations cumbersome, or abstract away the underlying error-correction schemes, reducing the effectiveness of resource utilization and estimation.   To address these limitations while preserving programmability, we present a quantum programming language that enables efficient resource utilization, together with a resource-estimation framework for comprehensive resource analysis. Our framework features programmer-visible abstractions of error-correction schemes and cross-layer program-hardware analysis, allowing systematic exploration of resource trade-offs. We evaluate our approach on detailed fault-tolerant implementations of practical large-scale quantum algorithms, including components typically treated as black boxes in existing frameworks. The results demonstrate that our framework enables substantial resource savings while delivering detailed, fine-grained, and accurate resource estimates for fault-tolerant quantum programs.
summary: This paper addresses the critical challenge of accurately estimating resources for fault-tolerant quantum algorithms. The authors propose a novel programming language and a cross-layer framework that allows programmers to explicitly manage error correction while enabling joint analysis of resource trade-offs. This results in significantly more accurate and detailed resource estimates compared to existing black-box methods.
main_problem: Resource estimation for fault-tolerant quantum computation is difficult because existing tools either force programmers to handle low-level hardware details or abstract away error correction schemes, leading to inaccurate resource utilization estimates.
main_result: The proposed framework enables substantial resource savings and provides detailed, fine-grained, and accurate resource estimates by jointly analyzing the logical program and its associated error-correction schemes.
method: The authors introduce a specialized quantum programming language and a cross-layer resource-estimation framework that allows programmers to define QEC schemes explicitly while enabling joint analysis across different abstraction layers.
model_or_system: The work focuses on Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation (FTQC), where logical qubits are encoded using physical qubits via Quantum Error-Correction Schemes ($\langle	ext{QEC}angle$). The framework models the compilation and execution flow from high-level logic down to hardware configuration.
key_observables: Space cost (# total physical qubits), Time cost (total runtime / syndrome-extraction cycles), and error rates (e.g., activate-operation vs. idle memory error).
important_parameters: Code distances ($d_{data}, d_{anc}$), the underlying physical error rate ($p_{phy} = 3 	imes 10^{-3}$), and mean decoding latency.
main_assumptions: The analysis requires a joint, cross-layer analysis of the program and QEC specifications, which is more complex than independent estimation methods. It also assumes that decoding latency can be utilized by inserting intermediate statements.

paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem limitations, presents the novel programming language and cross-layer framework, details the joint analysis methodology, evaluates it on practical large-scale algorithms, and concludes with resource savings demonstrations.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum computation theory, the systematic approach to resource accounting across multiple abstraction layers is highly relevant for developing robust simulation tools or understanding hardware overheads in any complex physical system modeled by layered control structures.
